64	function script(config: QueryScript = {}): void {
65	  queryMock.mockImplementation(({ options }) => {
66	    capturedOptions = options
67	    if (config.child !== undefined) {
68	      options.spawnClaudeCodeProcess?.({
69	        command: '/usr/bin/claude',
70	        args: [],
71	        cwd: process.cwd(),
72	        env: { PATH: '/usr/bin' },
73	      } as never)
74	    }
75	    const signal = options.abortController?.signal
76	    const iterator = (async function* published(): AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage> {
77	      for (const message of config.messages ?? []) {
78	        if (config.gapMs !== undefined) {
79	          // The real SDK settles promptly once its controller aborts; a mock
80	          // that ignored the signal would never exercise cancellation.
81	          await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
82	            const timer = setTimeout(resolve, config.gapMs)
83	            signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => {
84	              clearTimeout(timer)
85	              resolve()
86	            }, { once: true })
87	          })
88	        }
89	        if (signal?.aborted === true) throw new Error('the query was aborted')
90	        yield message
91	      }
92	      if (config.failWith !== undefined) throw config.failWith
93	    })()

95	      [Symbol.asyncIterator]: () => iterator,
96	      close: () => {
97	        closes()
98	        if (config.closeError !== undefined) throw config.closeError
99	      },
100	    } as unknown as Query
101	  })

92	export function request(overrides: Partial<GenerateOptions> = {}): GenerateOptions {
93	  return {
94	    provider: 'claude-code',
95	    model: 'default',

98	    ...overrides,

100	}

102	/** A three-message history: user turn, assistant tool call, tool result. */
103	export function toolConversation(): Message[] {
104	  const callId = CallId('call-1')
105	  return [
106	    createUserMessage({ source: { kind: 'user' }, content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'list the files' }] }),
107	    createAssistantMessage({
108	      source: { provider: 'claude-code', model: 'default' },
109	      content: [
110	        { type: 'text', text: 'Running it.' },
111	        { type: 'tool-call', id: callId, name: 'bash', arguments: '{"command":"ls"}' },
112	      ],
113	    }),
114	    createToolResultMessage({
115	      callId,
116	      isError: false,
117	      content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'a.txt\n' }],
118	    }),
119	  ]

122	/** Options for {@link fakeChild}. */
123	export interface FakeChildOptions {
124	  readonly pid?: number
125	  readonly waitForExitError?: Error
126	  readonly closeError?: Error
127	}
128	
129	/** A managed child under test control. */
130	export interface FakeChild {
131	  readonly handle: SubprocessHandle
132	  readonly stdin: PassThrough
133	  readonly stdout: PassThrough
134	  readonly settle: (outcome?: SubprocessOutcome) => void
135	  readonly fail: (error: Error) => void
136	  readonly terminate: Mock<SubprocessHandle['terminate']>
137	}
138	
139	/** Build a subprocess handle whose lifecycle a test drives directly. */
140	export function fakeChild(options: FakeChildOptions = {}): FakeChild {
141	  const stdin = new PassThrough()
142	  const stdout = new PassThrough()
143	  let exited = false
144	  let resolveDone!: (outcome: SubprocessOutcome) => void
145	  let rejectDone!: (error: Error) => void
146	  const done = new Promise<SubprocessOutcome>((resolve, reject) => {
147	    resolveDone = resolve
148	    rejectDone = reject
149	  })
150	  // Suites deliberately exercise rejected handles.
151	  void done.catch(() => {})
152	  const settle = (outcome: SubprocessOutcome = { exitCode: 0, signal: null }): void => {
153	    if (exited) return
154	    exited = true
155	    resolveDone(outcome)
156	  }
157	  const fail = (error: Error): void => {
158	    if (exited) return
159	    exited = true
160	    rejectDone(error)
161	  }
162	  const terminate = vi.fn<SubprocessHandle['terminate']>(() => { settle() })
163	  const handle: SubprocessHandle = {
164	    pid: options.pid ?? 4321,
165	    stdin,
166	    stdout,
167	    stderr: undefined,
168	    collected: {},
169	    done,
170	    terminate,
171	    waitForExit: vi.fn<SubprocessHandle['waitForExit']>(async () => {
172	      if (options.waitForExitError !== undefined) throw options.waitForExitError
173	      await done.catch(() => {})
174	      return true
175	    }),
176	  }
177	  return { handle, stdin, stdout, settle, fail, terminate }
178	}

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Serves the harness LLM seam from a Claude Code installation the operator has already authenticated, so a host with no API key can still run every harness role — implementer agents, validators, judges, program departments, workflow workers, in-process subagents — on that subscription.
6	
7	Every `generate()` on this route is one stateless query to that installation through the official Agent SDK. The harness system prompt becomes the query's system prompt, the conversation and the harness tool definitions become the query's prompt text, and the answer comes back as a structured output this package parses into the seam's `StreamChunk` protocol. The product runs no tool of its own and reads no workspace, so every tool call returns to the harness agent loop and executes under the harness's own tools, session log, read barrier, budget policy, and approvals.
8	
9	The package root exposes the Cordis plugin contract, `ClaudeCodeAdapter`, and the request/response helpers those two use; the SDK is a runtime dependency of this package, not of the seam.
10	
11	## Config
12	
13	```yaml
14	- id: llm-claude-code
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
16	  config:
17	    provider: claude-code    # required; the route registered on ctx.llm
18	    displayName: Claude Code # optional; the route name when omitted
19	    models:                  # required; a request naming any other model fails with UNKNOWN_MODEL
20	      - id: default          # the id harness requests select
21	        name: Claude Code default
22	        contextWindow: 200000 # optional; what the token meter and compaction threshold read
23	      # productModel names what the installation is asked to run; omit it and
24	      # the installation runs whatever it is configured to run.
25	      - id: fast
26	        productModel: <a model id this installation accepts>
27	    env:                     # optional; explicit entries over the scrubbed parent environment
28	      CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP: deepseek-harness/1
29	    effort: high             # optional; low | medium | high | xhigh | max
30	    thinking:                # optional; adaptive | enabled (with budgetTokens) | disabled
31	      type: adaptive
32	    queryTimeoutMs: 300000   # optional; maximum idle interval between messages of one query
33	    disposeGraceMs: 3000     # optional; CLI process-tree termination grace
34	    retryPolicy:             # optional; omission uses bounded normal defaults
35	      mode: normal
36	```
37	
38	`provider` is required and has no default: the route name is the composition's statement of which seam key this installation answers on, and two installations configured side by side must be able to name themselves differently.
39	
40	`models` is required and has no default either. The harness cannot interrogate an installation for the models its subscription entitles, so the catalog is operator configuration. `ctx.llm.listModels(provider)` returns these entries, `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, id)` returns the exact entry with its `contextWindow`, and — unlike the keyed adapters, whose catalogs are advisory — a request naming an unlisted model fails with `LlmError('UNKNOWN_MODEL')` before any query starts. Each entry declares `inputModalities: ['text']`, so image content is refused as a declared negative capability. An entry's optional `productModel` is passed to the installation as the product's `model` option; omitting it leaves that option off, which is the configuration a deployment wants when the installation's own default is the intended model.
41	
42	`effort` and `thinking` pass straight through to the query for every request on this route. They are route-level rather than per-request because this route publishes no reasoning efforts: a request that sets `GenerateOptions.reasoningEffort` fails with `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` at the seam.
43	
44	`queryTimeoutMs` bounds the gap between messages of one query, not the answer's duration. The query asks for partial assistant events, which arrive while the installation is still working, so the watchdog rearms on evidence of progress and only expires on a silent installation. Expiry throws `LlmError('TIMEOUT')`; an earlier caller abort throws `ABORTED`.
45	
46	## How a request is rendered
47	
48	The rendering is a pure function of the request the seam hands over, and that request is itself derived from the session log, so everything this package sends is reconstructable from the log. Two things enter the query:
49	
50	- **The system prompt.** `GenerateOptions.system` becomes the query's custom system prompt, replacing the product's own preset rather than appending to it. A request with no system prompt sends an empty one, which still replaces the preset.
51	- **The prompt text.** One reading-guide line, then the tool section when the request carries tools, then the whole conversation in log order. Each element is framed by tags prefixed `dsh-`: `<dsh-user>`, `<dsh-assistant>` with a nested `<dsh-tool-call id name>` per requested call, `<dsh-tool-result id status>` per result, and `<dsh-system>` for a system message that arrived inside the conversation. Attribute values are escaped; when any rendered content itself contains the prefix, the whole rendering moves to the first free numbered prefix (`dsh2-`, `dsh3-`, …), so no message can be read as framing.
52	
53	The query asks for a structured output of `{ content: string, toolCalls: [{ name, arguments }] }`, where `arguments` is the call's JSON object encoded as a JSON string — the form the seam carries end to end. Built-in tools, MCP servers, filesystem settings, and session persistence are all switched off (`tools: []`, `mcpServers: {}`, `strictMcpConfig: true`, `settingSources: []`, `persistSession: false`), and the permission mode never prompts and denies anything not pre-approved. The harness cancellation signal drives the SDK's abort controller, and the SDK-spawned CLI is placed under `ctx.subprocess`, which owns its process tree and termination ladder.
54	
55	The query's turn bound is two assistant messages. Offering no tools is what makes one `generate()` one model response; the bound is two rather than one because the product's structured-output delivery costs an assistant message of its own, so a reply that says anything before it needs both.
56	
57	## What comes back
58	
59	`structured_output` becomes the chunk stream: the visible text as one text block when it is non-empty, then one tool-call block per returned call, then usage, then the finish (`tool-calls` when the answer requested any, `stop` otherwise). Call ids are minted per response as `<result uuid>-<position>`, so they are unique across the session and stable for the tool result that answers them. Token counts map straight across — the product already reports uncached input separately from cache reads and writes, which is the seam's own disjoint convention.
60	
61	A missing or unreadable structured output is a provider failure, never an empty answer: `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`. An answer with neither text nor tool calls is `EMPTY_RESPONSE`, which the default retry policy retries.
62	
63	## Errors
64	
65	`UNKNOWN_MODEL` for a model the catalog does not declare, and `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` for image content, both before any query. `MISSING_EXECUTABLE` when the host has no `claude` on the subprocess seam's PATH. `TIMEOUT` and `ABORTED` for idle expiry and caller cancellation. `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` and `EMPTY_RESPONSE` for an unusable answer, and `STREAM_CLOSED` for a query that ended without publishing a result. A failed product result is classified from every code, terminal reason, stop reason, and message it carried: `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` and `QUOTA` through the seam's shared classifiers, then `MAX_TURNS`, `QUOTA`, `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, or `PRODUCT_ERROR` by result subtype. A failure the SDK raises by throwing rather than by publishing a result becomes `TRANSPORT` with the rendered cause chain in its message.
66	
67	## Model Experience
68	
69	### The query prompt
70	
71	#### What the model sees
72	
73	The installation's model reads the harness system prompt verbatim as its system prompt — inside an envelope of the product's own that this package neither authors nor can inspect, the one model-visible input here that the session log does not reconstruct — then a prompt text carrying the reading guide, the tool section, and the conversation. Named placeholders below stand for the request's own data: `{ns}` is the tag prefix (`dsh` unless content collides with it), `{tool name}`, `{tool description}`, and `{tool schema}` come from `GenerateOptions.tools`, and message text, call ids, and arguments come from the conversation.
74	
75	##### Verbatim guide and tool section
76	
77	```markdown
78	Answer the last turn of the conversation below. Elements tagged `<{ns}-…>` are the harness's framing; everything between them is the conversation.
79	<{ns}-tools>
80	The harness runs these tools, not you. Ask for a call by putting it in `toolCalls`; its result arrives in the next request.
81	<{ns}-tool name="{tool name}">
82	{tool description}
83	Arguments (JSON Schema):
84	{tool schema}
85	</{ns}-tool>
86	</{ns}-tools>
87	```
88	
89	#### Token effect
90	
91	The conversation and tool definitions are rendered on every request, so input grows with history exactly as it does on a keyed route, plus the fixed framing tags and the two guide sentences. The structured-output schema and the product's own envelope add a further fixed amount this package does not measure.
92	
93	#### KV Cache effect
94	
95	Each query is independent: the installation is asked for one stateless answer with no persisted session, so nothing this route sends reuses a prefix across turns. Cache reads and writes the product reports are passed through to the seam's usage, but this package makes no claim about which prefix produced them.
96	
97	### The structured answer
98	
99	#### What the model sees
100	
101	Nothing this package adds. The parsed text and tool calls become harness content blocks the agent loop logs and assembles, and the tool results the harness produces return in the next request's conversation.
102	
103	#### Token effect
104	
105	Generated tokens follow the route's configured effort and thinking policy; only the blocks the loop retains affect later input.
106	
107	#### KV Cache effect
108	
109	Retained response blocks append to the next request's rendered conversation. Because each query is stateless, that growth changes the next prompt rather than extending a reusable prefix.
110	
111	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
112	
113	- **No prompt caching across turns** — one `generate()` is one stateless query, so the whole conversation is re-sent and re-read every turn. A conversation that a keyed route would serve mostly from cache costs full input here, and latency per turn is the product's own start-up plus answer time.
114	- **The product's system-prompt envelope is not reconstructable from the session log** — the harness authors the system prompt, but the installation wraps it with text this package neither writes nor sees, so `request/header` records everything except that wrapper.
115	- **`maxTokens`, `temperature`, `topP`, `seed`, and `stop` are dropped** — the product's query options carry no equivalent, and the seam's contract is that an adapter whose wire has no equivalent drops the field.
116	- **No reasoning efforts are published** — `effort` and `thinking` are route-level configuration, so `agent/request` cannot vary reasoning per step the way it can on the keyed routes.
117	- **A product-side structured-output retry exceeds the turn bound** — the bound is two assistant messages, which covers one answer and its delivery; a retry surfaces as a failed query the harness retries as a whole request.
118	- **No settings-seam hot reload** — route facts resolve once at load, unlike the keyed adapters, which re-read a `ctx.settings` section per request. Adding it needs a settings namespace and the atomic route replacement the keyed adapters use.

# @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Serves ONE harness agent's own tool registry to an external agent as a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server, and executes every call it receives through `ctx.tools.execute()` on that agent. It is the inverse of [`dsh-mcp-client`](../mcp-client/README.md), which registers a foreign server's tools on `ctx.tools`: here a foreign model reaches the harness's tools instead, so approval, the registry guards, the filesystem policy each tool dispatches, the around-dispatch wrappers, and the durable `tool/call`/`tool/result` pair all apply to work a model outside this process asked for.

The [external-agent bridge Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-agent-bridge.md) owns the design rationale. Its first consumer is [`dsh-subagent-claude-code`](../../subagent/subagent-claude-code/README.md) in bridge mode.

## Usage

```yaml
- id: mcp-tool-server
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server'
  config:
    serverName: dsh
```

A consumer calls `instance(agent)`, hands the handle's `config` — `{ type: 'sdk', name, instance }`, the in-process server configuration an Agent SDK accepts verbatim — to whatever runs the external model under the handle's `serverName`, and awaits `dispose()` when the run ends. `toolNames` reports what was served, for the consumer's own record of the run.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `serverName` | `dsh` | MCP namespace a served run answers under when its request omits one. Matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`, because the consuming client qualifies every served tool as `mcp__<serverName>__<tool>`. |

`instance(agent, request)` takes the same namespace per run; `resolve(request)` is the one place that defaults it, and a namespace outside the pattern is refused there rather than at the first tool call.

## The served run is one turn

`tool/call` and `tool/result` are step-scoped events: the [session invariant](../../core/session/README.md) requires each to name the open turn and step. A handle therefore owns exactly one turn of the served agent's session — creation appends `turn/start` and `step/start`, `dispose()` appends `step/end` and `turn/end` — which is what makes an external agent's calls durable at all. It is also the honest record: an external agent's run IS one turn of the harness session that authorized it.

That holds because the served agent is a child created for one run and driven by nobody else. Serving an agent whose session already has a turn open is refused at `instance()`, as is a second live run on one agent. Plugin disposal releases every run the service still owns, so a disposed composition leaves no open turn behind.

## What a served call actually does

The tool list is the agent's own registry view (`ctx.tools.schemas(agent)`), snapshotted at `instance()`: it is what the external model plans against and what a consumer's durable record names, so a set that changed underneath it would make both wrong. Names are served verbatim; the `mcp__<serverName>__` qualification is the consuming client's.

A `tools/call` appends `tool/call`, awaits `ctx.tools.execute({ callId, name, arguments, agent, signal })`, appends `tool/result` citing that call, and returns the executor's rendered content. A name outside the served snapshot is refused, and would still fail `UNKNOWN_TOOL` at the executor if it were reached: the list is presentation, the executor is the authority.

## Model Experience

### The served tool list

#### What the model sees

The external model sees one MCP tool per tool the served agent sees, with the harness description and JSON Schema verbatim. It sees no harness prompt, no persona, and no session history — the served surface is tools and nothing else.

#### Token effect

The external product pays for those schemas in its own context. Nothing is added to any harness model's context.

#### KV Cache effect

Independent of every harness request cache. The snapshot is fixed for the life of the run, so the external product's own prefix stays stable across its turns.

### The result of a served call

#### What the model sees

The tool's model-facing content, flattened to one text payload — the same projection a harness model would receive. A non-text block is named rather than dropped, and an executor failure (a denial, a guard, a tool error) arrives as an MCP error result carrying that message.

141	 * ordinary durable pair. Every authority the harness has — approval, guards,
142	 * the filesystem policy each tool dispatches, the around-dispatch wrappers,
143	 * the content projection — applies because this is the same `execute` call the
144	 * agent loop makes.
145	 * @param call - the run's registry, agent, namespace, and turn position.
146	 * @param name - the harness tool name the client asked for.
147	 * @param args - the client's arguments, already defaulted for an argumentless call.
148	 * @param callId - the identity shared by the durable call/result pair.
149	 * @param signal - the client's cancellation for this request.
150	 * @returns the executor's outcome after both durable events are appended.
151	 */
152	export async function executeServedCall(
153	  call: ServedCallContext,
154	  name: string,
155	  args: Record<string, unknown>,
156	  callId: CallId,
157	  signal: AbortSignal,
158	): Promise<ToolExecutionResult> {
159	  const session = call.agent.session
160	  const { turn, step } = call.position
161	  const started = session.append('tool/call', {
162	    turn,
163	    step,
164	    callId,
165	    name,
166	    arguments: JSON.stringify(args),
167	  })
168	  const result = await call.ctx.tools.execute({ callId, name, arguments: args, agent: call.agent, signal })
169	  session.append('tool/result', {
170	    turn,
171	    step,
172	    message: createToolResultMessage({ callId, content: result.content, isError: result.isError }),
173	    ...result.error?.info ? { error: result.error.info } : {},
174	    ...result.meta !== undefined ? { meta: result.meta } : {},
175	  }, { surfaceOp: 'append', sourceEventSeqs: [started.seq] })
176	  return result
177	}
178	
179	/** One live served server with the state its handlers read. */
180	export interface ServedServer {
181	  /** The official MCP server the consumer connects a transport to. */
182	  readonly instance: McpServer
183	  /** The tool names served, snapshotted when the server was built. */
184	  readonly toolNames: readonly string[]
185	  /** Stop answering calls; later requests fail with the closed-run error. */
186	  close(): void
187	}
188	
189	/**
190	 * Build one agent's MCP server. The tool list is snapshotted here: it is what
191	 * the external model plans against and what the run's durable record names, so
192	 * a set that changed underneath it would make both wrong.
193	 * @param call - the run's registry, agent, namespace, and turn position.
194	 * @param spec - the resolved server inputs.
195	 * @returns the server and the names it serves.
196	 */
197	export function buildServedServer(call: ServedCallContext, spec: McpToolServerSpec): ServedServer {
198	  const tools = servedTools(call.ctx, call.agent)
199	  const names = new Set(tools.map(tool => tool.name))
200	  const instance = new McpServer(
201	    { name: spec.serverName, version: MCP_TOOL_SERVER_VERSION },
202	    { capabilities: { tools: {} } },
203	  )
204	  let calls = 0
205	  let closed = false
206	  const requireOpen = (): void => {
207	    if (closed) {
208	      throw new Error(`mcp-tool-server(${spec.serverName}): the served run is over; no further tool calls are accepted`)
209	    }
210	  }
211	  // The low-level request handlers, not `registerTool`: harness tools carry
212	  // JSON Schema, and the high-level registration takes a Zod shape instead.
213	  instance.server.setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, () => {
214	    requireOpen()
215	    return { tools }
216	  })
217	  instance.server.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, async (request, extra) => {
218	    requireOpen()
219	    const name = request.params.name
220	    // A name outside the served snapshot is refused here AND would fail
221	    // `UNKNOWN_TOOL` at the executor: the list is presentation, the executor is
222	    // the authority, and neither stands alone.
223	    if (!names.has(name)) {
224	      throw new Error(`mcp-tool-server(${spec.serverName}): "${name}" is not a tool of this agent`)
225	    }
226	    const result = await executeServedCall(
227	      call,
228	      name,
229	      // An argumentless MCP call omits the member; the executor requires
230	      // lossless JSON, and `{}` is what an empty argument list means.
231	      request.params.arguments ?? {},
232	      CallId(`${spec.serverName}:${++calls}`),
233	      extra.signal,
234	    )
235	    return { content: [{ type: 'text' as const, text: resultText(result.content, name) }], isError: result.isError }
236	  })
237	  return {
238	    instance,
239	    toolNames: tools.map(tool => tool.name),
240	    close(): void {
241	      closed = true
242	    },
243	  }
244	}

1	/**
2	 * Bridge mode: the external agent runs on the harness's own tools and nothing
3	 * else. This module owns the child harness agent it runs as, the SDK options
4	 * that pin its tool surface shut, and the fold from the SDK message stream into
5	 * the child session's durable record.
6	 *
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code/bridge
8	 */
9	
10	import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
11	import type { Options, PermissionResult, SDKMessage } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk'
12	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import type { Agent, AgentHandle } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
14	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	import type { McpToolServerHandle } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server'
16	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
17	import type { Session, SessionEventMap } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import {
19	  applyChildComposition,
20	  appendDelegatedPolicyOverrides,
21	  captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides,
22	  childSessionMeta,
23	  resolveChildAgentOptions,
24	  resolveChildDepth,
25	  SubagentError,
26	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
27	import type { ResolvedSubagentStartRequest, SubagentStopReason } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
28	import type { BridgeAssistantData, BridgeEndData, BridgeStartData } from './types.ts'
29	
30	/** MCP namespace the bridged server answers under, and the prefix its tools carry. */
31	export const BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME = 'dsh'
32	
33	/** The only tool-name prefix a bridged external model may call. */
34	export const BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX = `mcp__${BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME}__`
35	
36	/** Refusal a bridged run answers every tool outside the harness namespace with. */
37	export const BRIDGE_TOOL_DENIAL = 'this run may only call the harness tools served under '
38	  + `"${BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX}"`
39	
40	/**
41	 * Code carried by the refusal to bridge without the tool server composed, so a
42	 * caller routes it without parsing the message.
43	 */
44	export const SUBAGENT_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE = 'BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE'
45	
46	/**
47	 * Read the token accounting an SDK message reports. The stream crosses a
48	 * process boundary, so each field is accepted only as a number and a partial
49	 * report yields none rather than a fabricated zero.
50	 * @param usage - the SDK's usage record, whatever it carried.
51	 * @returns the harness token accounting, or `undefined` when the product reported none.
52	 */
53	export function bridgeUsage(usage: unknown): TokenUsage | undefined {
54	  if (typeof usage !== 'object' || usage === null) return undefined
55	  const record = usage as Record<string, unknown>
56	  const input = record['input_tokens']
57	  const output = record['output_tokens']
58	  if (typeof input !== 'number' || typeof output !== 'number') return undefined
59	  const cacheRead = record['cache_read_input_tokens']
60	  const cacheWrite = record['cache_creation_input_tokens']
61	  return {
62	    inputTokens: input,
63	    outputTokens: output,
64	    ...typeof cacheRead === 'number' ? { cacheReadTokens: cacheRead } : {},
65	    ...typeof cacheWrite === 'number' ? { cacheWriteTokens: cacheWrite } : {},
66	  }
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * Project one SDK assistant message onto its durable record. Text blocks only:
71	 * the tool calls in the same message are already the executor's `tool/call`
72	 * events.
73	 * @param message - one message from the SDK stream.
74	 * @returns the payload to append, or `undefined` when the message carries no text.
75	 */
76	export function bridgeAssistantRecord(message: SDKMessage): BridgeAssistantData | undefined {
77	  if (message.type !== 'assistant') return undefined
78	  const blocks = message.message.content
79	  const text = blocks
80	    .flatMap(block => (block.type === 'text' ? [block.text] : []))
81	    .join('')
82	  if (text.length === 0) return undefined
83	  const usage = bridgeUsage(message.message.usage)
84	  return { text, ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage } }
85	}

87	/**

89	 * surface. `tools` and `allowedTools` decide what the model is told about;
90	 * `canUseTool` is the fence, because a model that names something else anyway
91	 * is denied in the operation that would run it.
92	 * @param server - the in-process MCP server configuration serving the child's registry.
93	 * @param maxTurns - the caller's turn ceiling, when one was requested.
94	 * @returns the options merged over the provider's ordinary query options.
95	 */
96	export function bridgeQueryOptions(
97	  server: McpToolServerHandle['config'],
98	  maxTurns: number | undefined,
99	): Partial<Options> {
100	  return {
101	    tools: [],
102	    mcpServers: { [BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME]: server },
103	    allowedTools: [`${BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX}*`],
104	    strictMcpConfig: true,
105	    settingSources: [],
106	    canUseTool: (toolName: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<PermissionResult> =>
107	      Promise.resolve(toolName.startsWith(BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX)

110	    ...maxTurns === undefined ? {} : { maxTurns },

115	export interface BridgedRun {

117	  readonly agent: Agent
118	  /** The child's session id, which is also the run id. */
119	  readonly id: SessionId
120	  /** SDK options pinning the external model to the served harness tools. */
121	  readonly options: Partial<Options>

123	  observe(message: SDKMessage): void

127	  release(): Promise<void>

131	export interface BridgeInputs {
132	  /** The provider's plugin context, where the tool server resolves. */
133	  readonly ctx: Context
134	  /** The resolved one-shot request, whose parent supplies lineage and composition. */
135	  readonly request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest
136	  /** The provider name recorded in the run's opening event. */
137	  readonly provider: string

142	 * advertises the capability without composing the server is a misconfiguration,
143	 * and the earliest point that can see it is the start it would silently
144	 * degrade.
145	 * @param ctx - the provider's plugin context.
146	 * @returns the tool-server service.
147	 * @throws {@link SubagentError} with {@link SUBAGENT_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE} when none is composed.
148	 */
149	function requireToolServer(ctx: Context) {
150	  const server = ctx.get('mcpToolServer')
151	  if (server === undefined) {
152	    throw new SubagentError(
153	      'subagent-claude-code: harnessTools requires @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server in the composition',
154	      SUBAGENT_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE,
155	    )
156	  }
157	  return server
158	}

160	/** The three log-only events this package owns. */
161	interface BridgeEventMap {
162	  'bridge/start': BridgeStartData
163	  'bridge/assistant': BridgeAssistantData
164	  'bridge/end': BridgeEndData
165	}
166	
167	/**
168	 * Narrow the generic append face to this package's own events, which
169	 * discharges `Session.append`'s conditional surface-options tuple: all three
170	 * are log-only.
171	 * @param session - the child session recording the run.
172	 * @returns the narrowed append function.
173	 */
174	function bridgeRecorder(session: Session) {
175	  return session.append.bind(session) as <Event extends keyof BridgeEventMap>(
176	    event: Event,
177	    value: SessionEventMap[Event],
178	  ) => void
179	}
180	
181	/**
182	 * Create the child harness agent, serve its tools, and open the run's durable
183	 * record. Rejection leaves nothing published: the agent factory's creation
184	 * transaction rolls back, and a failure after publication releases the child
185	 * before rethrowing.
186	 * @param inputs - the provider context, the resolved request, and the provider name.
187	 * @returns the live bridge the run is driven through.
188	 */
189	export async function openBridgedRun(inputs: BridgeInputs): Promise<BridgedRun> {
190	  const { ctx, request, provider } = inputs
191	  const toolServer = requireToolServer(ctx)
192	  const parent = request.parent
193	  const childDepth = resolveChildDepth(parent, request.maxDepth)
194	  const childId = SessionId(randomUUID())
195	  // Captured before the first await: a later parent switch belongs to the
196	  // parent's future, not to this child.
197	  const inherited = captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides(parent)
198	
199	  const handle: AgentHandle = await parent.ctx.agents.create({
200	    sessionId: childId,
201	    meta: childSessionMeta(parent, childDepth, 0),
202	    agentOptions: resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, request.agentOptions, childDepth),
203	    signal: request.signal,
204	    setup: (childCtx: Context): void => {
205	      appendDelegatedPolicyOverrides((childCtx.agent as Agent).session, inherited)
206	      // The composition carries no per-child persona or tool filter: this
207	      // provider advertises neither capability, so the service has already
208	      // rejected a request that asked for one.
209	      applyChildComposition(childCtx, parent, {})
210	      ;(childCtx.agent as Agent).session.append('subagent/descriptor', request.descriptor)
211	    },
212	  })
213	
214	  const agent = handle.agent
215	  let served: McpToolServerHandle
216	  try {
217	    served = toolServer.instance(agent, { serverName: BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME })
218	  } catch (error: unknown) {
219	    await handle.dispose()
220	    throw error
221	  }
222	
223	  const record = bridgeRecorder(agent.session)
224	  record('bridge/start', {
225	    provider,
226	    tools: served.toolNames.map(name => `${BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX}${name}`),
227	  })
228	
229	  let settled = false
230	  let lastUsage: TokenUsage | undefined
231	  let released: Promise<void> | undefined
232	  const settle = (stopReason: SubagentStopReason): void => {
233	    if (settled) return
234	    settled = true
235	    record('bridge/end', { stopReason, ...lastUsage === undefined ? {} : { usage: lastUsage } })
236	  }
237	
238	  return {
239	    agent,
240	    id: childId,
241	    options: bridgeQueryOptions(served.config, request.agentOptions?.maxTurns),
242	    observe(message: SDKMessage): void {
243	      if (message.type === 'result') lastUsage = bridgeUsage(message.usage) ?? lastUsage
244	      const assistant = bridgeAssistantRecord(message)
245	      if (assistant !== undefined) record('bridge/assistant', assistant)
246	    },
247	    settle,
248	    release(): Promise<void> {
249	      if (released !== undefined) return released
250	      // The run's record closes before the served turn does, so `bridge/end`
251	      // always lands inside the turn its tool calls occupy.
252	      settle('aborted')
253	      released = served.dispose().then(() => handle.dispose())
254	      return released
255	    },
256	  }
257	}

10	 * human-readable `message`, and supports `cause` chaining via the standard
11	 * `ErrorOptions`. `name` defaults to the subclass constructor name.

14	  /** Stable machine-routable failure class (e.g. `RATE_LIMIT`); route on this, never by parsing `message`. */

18	    super(message, options)

31	 * Canonical provider-neutral code for a response that completed normally but
32	 * carried no content blocks at all. Providers occasionally emit a degenerate
33	 * completion (a terminal stop with zero output); adapters classify it as this
34	 * failure instead of yielding an empty assistant message, because an empty
35	 * message silently ends the turn with nothing for the user or the loop to act
36	 * on. The attempt produced nothing durable, so retry policy treats it as safe

44	 * `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` because the fix differs: correct the stored value
45	 * rather than supply one. Deliberately outside the default retryable set —
46	 * a malformed credential fails identically on every attempt.

60	  + String.raw`too\s+(?:large|long)\s+for\s+(?:(?:this|the)\s+)?`
61	  + String.raw`(?:model(?:'s)?\s+)?context(?:\s+window)?\b`,

68	  + String.raw`\b(?:exceed(?:s|ed)?|overflows?|is\s+larger\s+than)\b.{0,40}`

75	 * and library adapters. Adapters pass all available provider code, type, and
76	 * message text so both thrown and in-band delivery styles share one classifier.
77	 * @param detail - provider error code/type/message text joined into one string.
78	 * @returns true when the detail identifies a request exceeding the model context window.
79	 */

81	  return STRUCTURED_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW.test(detail)
82	    || /\b(?:maximum|max)(?:\s+(?:allowed|supported))?\s+context\s+(?:length|window)\b/i.test(detail)
83	    || TOO_LARGE_FOR_CONTEXT.test(detail)
84	    || /\b(?:input|prompt|request)\s+(?:is\s+)?too\s+(?:long|large)\s+for\s+(?:this|the)\s+model\b/i.test(detail)

90	 * than a transient request-rate limit.
91	 * @param detail - provider error code/type/message text joined into one string.
92	 * @returns true only for terminal quota, balance, credit, budget, or usage-limit wording.
93	 */
94	export function isQuotaExceededError(detail: string): boolean {
95	  return /\binsufficient[\s_-]+(?:quota|balance|credits?)\b/i.test(detail)
96	    || /\b(?:quota|usage[\s_-]+limit)[\s_-]+(?:exceeded|exhausted|reached)\b/i.test(detail)
97	    || /\bexceed(?:ed|s)?[\s_-]+(?:(?:your|the)[\s_-]+)?(?:current[\s_-]+)?quota\b/i.test(detail)
98	    || /\b(?:balance|credits?)[\s_-]+(?:exhausted|depleted)\b/i.test(detail)
99	    || /\bout[\s_-]+of[\s_-]+(?:credits?|budget)\b/i.test(detail)
100	}

102	/**
103	 * Render a thrown value with its full `cause` chain and AggregateError
104	 * members, so transport wrappers like undici's `TypeError: fetch failed`
105	 * surface the underlying failure instead of masking it. Plain structured
106	 * failures render their own data-backed `message`. Diagnostic-surface
107	 * rendering only (messages, notices, logs) — never parse the result; route on
108	 * {@link HarnessError.code}.
109	 * @param value - the caught value (`unknown` in catch clauses).
110	 * @returns the outermost message first, each cause appended with `: ` (skipped
111	 * when it repeats the wrapper message verbatim), and AggregateError members
112	 * bracketed and `; `-joined.
113	 */
114	export function errorChain(value: unknown): string {
115	  // Tracks the active recursion path (entries removed on exit), so only true
116	  // cycles are flagged and a diamond-shared cause still renders in full.
117	  const path = new Set<unknown>()
118	  const render = (current: unknown): string => {
119	    if (path.has(current)) return '<circular cause>'
120	    path.add(current)
121	    try {
122	      if (!(current instanceof Error)) {
123	        if (typeof current === 'object' && current !== null) {
124	          const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(current, 'message')
125	          if (descriptor !== undefined && 'value' in descriptor && typeof descriptor.value === 'string') {
126	            return descriptor.value
127	          }
128	        }
129	        return String(current)
130	      }
131	      const message = current.message === '' ? current.name : current.message
132	      const members = current instanceof AggregateError && current.errors.length > 0
133	        ? ` [${current.errors.map(render).join('; ')}]`
134	        : ''
135	      const causeText = current.cause === undefined || current.cause === null
136	        ? ''
137	        : render(current.cause)
138	      // Wrappers like `new HarnessError(String(value), code, { cause: value })`
139	      // repeat their cause verbatim; rendering it again would only add noise.
140	      const cause = causeText === '' || causeText === message ? '' : `: ${causeText}`
141	      return `${message}${members}${cause}`
142	    } catch {
143	      // Only hostile coercion or hostile accessors (a throwing toString /
144	      // Symbol.toPrimitive on a non-Error, or a throwing message/name/cause/
145	      // errors getter on an Error subclass): this renderer feeds UI notices
146	      // and logs, so nothing may escape. Inner frames catch their own throws,
147	      // so only the hostile node collapses, not the whole chain.
148	      return '<unrenderable value>'
149	    } finally {
150	      path.delete(current)
151	    }
152	  }
153	  return render(value)
154	}

156	/**
157	 * Narrow an arbitrary thrown value to a HarnessError (for `instanceof` at runtime boundaries).
158	 * @param value - the caught value (`unknown` in catch clauses).
159	 * @returns true only for real instances; duck-typed or cross-realm errors do not narrow.
160	 */
161	export function isHarnessError(value: unknown): value is HarnessError {
162	  return value instanceof HarnessError
163	}

2	 * Normalization for values thrown by a final LLM adapter boundary.
3	 *
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/adapter-failure

6	
7	import { HarnessError } from './error.ts'
8	import type { LlmFailure } from './types.ts'
9	
10	/**
11	 * Detach serializable provider facts from a value thrown by an adapter.
12	 * @param value - arbitrary value thrown during adapter dispatch or iteration.
13	 * @returns immutable provider-neutral facts suitable for a terminal finish chunk.
14	 * @internal
15	 */
16	export function normalizeLlmFailure(value: unknown): LlmFailure {
17	  const error = value instanceof Error
18	    ? value
19	    : new HarnessError(thrownMessage(value), 'UNKNOWN', { cause: value })
20	  // Cross-package copies preserve own data but not class identity. Trust the
21	  // carried facts only when both own properties agree after validation.
22	  const carried = ownFailureSnapshot(error)
23	  if (carried !== undefined && carried.code === ownErrorCode(error)) return carried
24	  return Object.freeze({
25	    message: errorMessage(error),
26	    code: harnessErrorCode(error),
27	  })
28	}
29	
30	/** Render a non-Error throw without letting hostile coercion escape normalization. */
31	function thrownMessage(value: unknown): string {
32	  try {
33	    const message = String(value)
34	    return message.length > 0 ? message : 'LLM adapter failed'
35	  } catch (_hostileThrownValue) {
36	    return 'LLM adapter failed'
37	  }
38	}
39	
40	/** Read a foreign error's own data-backed `code` without invoking accessors. */
41	function ownErrorCode(error: Error): unknown {
42	  try {
43	    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(error, 'code')
44	    return descriptor !== undefined && 'value' in descriptor ? descriptor.value : undefined
45	  } catch (_sdkPropertyTrap) {
46	    return undefined
47	  }
48	}
49	
50	/** Snapshot an own data property without invoking an SDK-defined accessor. */
51	function ownFailureSnapshot(error: Error): LlmFailure | undefined {
52	  try {
53	    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(error, 'failure')
54	    return descriptor !== undefined && 'value' in descriptor
55	      ? failureSnapshot(descriptor.value)
56	      : undefined
57	  } catch (_sdkPropertyTrap) {
58	    return undefined
59	  }
60	}
61	
62	/** Validate and detach an arbitrary serializable failure payload. */
63	function failureSnapshot(value: unknown): LlmFailure | undefined {
64	  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined
65	  try {
66	    const candidate = value as Partial<LlmFailure>
67	    const message = candidate.message
68	    const code = candidate.code
69	    const status = candidate.status
70	    const providerRetryAfterMs = candidate.providerRetryAfterMs
71	    const requestId = candidate.requestId
72	    if (typeof message !== 'string' || message.length === 0
73	      || typeof code !== 'string' || code.length === 0
74	      || (status !== undefined && (!Number.isInteger(status) || status < 100 || status > 599))
75	      || (providerRetryAfterMs !== undefined
76	        && (!Number.isFinite(providerRetryAfterMs) || providerRetryAfterMs <= 0))
77	      || (requestId !== undefined && (typeof requestId !== 'string' || requestId.length === 0))) return undefined
78	    return Object.freeze({
79	      message,
80	      code,
81	      ...status === undefined ? {} : { status },
82	      ...providerRetryAfterMs === undefined ? {} : { providerRetryAfterMs },
83	      ...requestId === undefined ? {} : { requestId },
84	    })
85	  } catch (_sdkFailureGetter) {
86	    return undefined
87	  }
88	}
89	
90	/** Read an SDK error message without letting an accessor replace the primary failure. */
91	function errorMessage(error: Error): string {
92	  try {
93	    const message: unknown = error.message
94	    if (typeof message === 'string' && message.length > 0) return message
95	  } catch (_sdkMessageGetter) {
96	    // The fallback below preserves a serializable failure beside the original Error.
97	  }
98	  return 'LLM adapter failed'
99	}
100	
101	/** Trust only Harness-owned codes; third-party SDK codes are not our taxonomy. */
102	function harnessErrorCode(error: Error): string {
103	  return error instanceof HarnessError ? error.code : 'UNKNOWN'
104	}

1	/**
2	 * The MCP tool server (`ctx.mcpToolServer`): serves ONE harness agent's own
3	 * tool registry to an external agent over MCP, and executes every call it
4	 * receives through `ctx.tools.execute()` on that agent. It is the inverse of
5	 * [`dsh-mcp-client`](../../mcp-client/README.md), which registers a foreign
6	 * server's tools on `ctx.tools`; here a foreign model reaches the harness's
7	 * tools instead, so approval, guards, the filesystem policy, the timeout
8	 * wrappers, and the durable `tool/call`/`tool/result` pair all apply to work a
9	 * model outside this process asked for.
10	 *
11	 * A served run is one turn of the served agent's session — the step-scoped
12	 * durable pair needs one — so the agent handed to {@link
13	 * McpToolServerService.instance} must be a child nothing else drives. The
14	 * [external-agent bridge Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-agent-bridge.md)
15	 * owns the design rationale.
16	 *
17	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server
18	 */
19	
20	import type { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js'
21	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
22	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
23	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
24	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
25	// Side-effect type import: declaration-merges `ctx.tools` onto Context.
26	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
27	import { buildServedServer, closeServedTurn, openServedTurn } from './server.ts'
28	import type { McpToolServerRequest, McpToolServerSpec } from './types.ts'
29	
30	export type * from './types.ts'
31	export { MCP_TOOL_SERVER_VERSION } from './server.ts'
32	
33	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
34	  interface Context {
35	    mcpToolServer: McpToolServerService
36	  }
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * Valid `serverName`. The consuming client qualifies every served tool as
41	 * `mcp__<serverName>__<tool>`, so the namespace must survive that composition
42	 * as an ordinary function name.
43	 */
44	const SERVER_NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/
45	
46	/** Default MCP namespace, which the shipped bridge consumer names in its allowlist. */
47	export const DEFAULT_SERVER_NAME = 'dsh'
48	
49	/**
50	 * The in-process server configuration an Agent SDK accepts verbatim. It is the
51	 * MCP SDK's own `McpServer` behind the two identity fields such an SDK reads.
52	 */
53	export interface McpToolServerInstanceConfig {
54	  /** Selects the in-process transport rather than a spawned or remote server. */
55	  readonly type: 'sdk'
56	  /** The resolved MCP namespace. */
57	  readonly name: string
58	  /** The live server; not serializable. */
59	  readonly instance: McpServer
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * One live served run. The consumer connects {@link config} to its external
64	 * agent, and MUST {@link dispose} it: disposal closes the run's turn, which is
65	 * what makes the served agent's log well-formed.
66	 */
67	export interface McpToolServerHandle {
68	  /** The resolved MCP namespace this server answers under. */
69	  readonly serverName: string
70	  /** The agent every served call runs as, and whose session records the run. */
71	  readonly serves: Agent
72	  /** The in-process configuration to hand an Agent SDK. */
73	  readonly config: McpToolServerInstanceConfig
74	  /** The harness tool names served, snapshotted at creation. */
75	  readonly toolNames: readonly string[]
76	  /**
77	   * Close the transport, refuse every later call, and close the run's turn.
78	   * Idempotent.
79	   * @returns fulfillment after the server released its transport.
80	   */
81	  dispose(): Promise<void>
82	}
83	
84	/** Deployment-owned MCP identity of the served registry. */
85	export interface Config {
86	  /**
87	   * MCP namespace a served run answers under when its request omits one
88	   * (default `dsh`). Matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`.
89	   */
90	  serverName?: string
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * The MCP tool server service. One instance serves any number of agents; each
95	 * `instance()` call owns one run, and one agent may hold only one live run.
96	 */
97	export class McpToolServerService extends Service {
98	  static inject = ['tools']
99	
100	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
101	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
102	    serverName: z.string().pattern(SERVER_NAME_PATTERN).default(DEFAULT_SERVER_NAME),
103	  })
104	
105	  /** Live runs keyed by served agent, so a second concurrent run fails loud. */
106	  private readonly live = new Map<SessionId, McpToolServerHandle>()
107	
108	  /** The schema-defaulted configuration; every field is present after validation. */
109	  private readonly config: Required<Config>
110	
111	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
112	    super(ctx, 'mcpToolServer')
113	    this.config = config as Required<Config>
114	    // A disposed plugin must leave no run's turn open, so releasing the live
115	    // runs is an effect of this service rather than a consumer's obligation.
116	    ctx.effect(() => () => this.releaseLive(), 'mcp-tool-server.runs')
117	  }
118	
119	  /**
120	   * Release every run this service still owns. A consumer that disposed its
121	   * own handle leaves nothing for this to do.
122	   */
123	  private async releaseLive(): Promise<void> {
124	    await Promise.all([...this.live.values()].map(handle => handle.dispose()))
125	  }
126	
127	  /**
128	   * Resolve one request against the deployment's configuration. Defaulting
129	   * happens here and nowhere else, so a caller reading a resolved spec sees
130	   * exactly what the run uses.
131	   * @param request - the caller's optional namespace override.
132	   * @returns the resolved server inputs.
133	   */
134	  resolve(request: McpToolServerRequest): McpToolServerSpec {
135	    const serverName = request.serverName ?? this.config.serverName
136	    if (!SERVER_NAME_PATTERN.test(serverName)) {
137	      throw new Error(`mcp-tool-server: serverName ${JSON.stringify(serverName)} must match ${String(SERVER_NAME_PATTERN)}`)
138	    }
139	    return { serverName }
140	  }
141	
142	  /**
143	   * Serve one agent's tools as an in-process MCP server and open the turn its
144	   * calls are recorded in.
145	   * @param agent - the agent whose registry view is served and whose session records the run.
146	   * @param request - optional namespace override for this run.
147	   * @returns the handle carrying the SDK configuration, the served names, and disposal.
148	   * @throws when that agent already holds a live run, or when its session has a turn open.
149	   */
150	  instance(agent: Agent, request: McpToolServerRequest = {}): McpToolServerHandle {
151	    const spec = this.resolve(request)
152	    const existing = this.live.get(agent.id)
153	    if (existing !== undefined) {
154	      throw new Error(
155	        `mcp-tool-server(${spec.serverName}): agent "${agent.id}" already holds a live served run`
156	        + ' — dispose it before serving that agent again',
157	      )
158	    }
159	    const position = openServedTurn(agent.session, spec.serverName)
160	    const served = buildServedServer({ ctx: this.ctx, agent, serverName: spec.serverName, position }, spec)
161	    let disposal: Promise<void> | undefined
162	    const handle: McpToolServerHandle = {
163	      serverName: spec.serverName,
164	      serves: agent,
165	      config: { type: 'sdk', name: spec.serverName, instance: served.instance },
166	      toolNames: served.toolNames,
167	      dispose: (): Promise<void> => {
168	        if (disposal !== undefined) return disposal
169	        served.close()
170	        this.live.delete(agent.id)
171	        disposal = served.instance.close().finally(() => { closeServedTurn(agent.session, position) })
172	        return disposal
173	      },
174	    }
175	    this.live.set(agent.id, handle)
176	    return handle
177	  }
178	}
179	
180	export default McpToolServerService

# Agent Note: the LLM seam served by a local Claude Code installation

Status: proposed

English | [中文](2026-09-06-llm-claude-code.zh.md)

## Problem

The harness is model-agnostic at the LLM seam, but both shipped providers need an API key: [`dsh-llm-deepseek`](../../../../packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md) resolves `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and [`dsh-llm-pi-ai`](../../../../packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md) resolves one credential per configured route. A host with no key and a Claude Code installation the operator has already authenticated can therefore run no harness role at all through the seam.

That installation can already enter the harness, but only through the subagent seam, where [`dsh-subagent-claude-code`](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/README.md) hands it a whole delegated task. Everything the harness owns is then out of reach for the work that task performs: the product picks its own tools, its own file access, its own loop, and its own session, and the harness sees one opaque answer. Nothing about the operator's subscription requires that trade — only the absence of a provider that speaks the LLM seam.

## Proposal

Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code`: a Service Provider on the LLM seam whose every `generate()` is one stateless query to the operator's installation through the pinned official Agent SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`), the same dependency and the same process ownership the subagent provider already uses.

One plugin instance registers one route on `ctx.llm`. The route name is a required `Config` field with no default, and the model catalog is required configuration too: the harness cannot interrogate an installation for the models its subscription entitles, so only the operator can say. Unlike the keyed adapters, whose catalogs are advisory, a request naming an unlisted model fails with `UNKNOWN_MODEL` before any query starts, because an unlisted id here has no meaning to pass through to. A catalog entry's optional `productModel` is what the query asks the installation to run; omitting it leaves the option off so the installation runs whatever it is configured to run.

Each request renders into two query inputs. The harness system prompt becomes the query's custom system prompt, replacing the product's own preset. The conversation and the harness tool definitions become one prompt text: a reading-guide line, a tool section, then every message in log order, framed by `dsh-`-prefixed tags with escaped attribute values. When rendered content itself contains the prefix, the whole rendering moves to the first free numbered prefix, so no message can be read as framing. The answer is requested as a structured output of `{ content, toolCalls: [{ name, arguments }] }`, with `arguments` a JSON string — the form the seam carries end to end.

The product therefore executes nothing. `tools: []`, `mcpServers: {}`, `strictMcpConfig: true`, `settingSources: []`, and `persistSession: false` leave it one prompt and one schema; the permission mode never prompts and denies anything not pre-approved. Every tool call comes back as a seam chunk, and the harness agent loop executes it under the harness's own tools, session log, read barrier, budget policy, and approvals — which is the whole point of putting this at the LLM seam rather than the subagent seam.

The SDK-spawned CLI goes under `ctx.subprocess` through the same custom-spawn projection the subagent provider uses, so the harness owns the process tree, its environment scrub, and its termination ladder. The harness cancellation signal drives the SDK's abort controller.

### The turn bound

The query asks for `maxTurns: 2`, counted in assistant messages. What makes one `generate()` one model response is offering no tools: the product can speak and then deliver its structured answer, and it can never act between turns. The bound is two rather than one because the delivery costs an assistant message of its own — a one-turn bound refuses every reply that says anything before delivering, which is most of them. It is fixed rather than configurable because it belongs to the product's structured-output protocol, not to a deployment.

### What is logged

The rendering is a pure function of the messages the seam hands over, and those messages are themselves derived from the session log, so every model-visible input this process authors is reconstructable from the log — the [reconstructability](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-05-reconstructable-requests.md) property holds unchanged.

One input is outside that: the product wraps the supplied system prompt with an envelope of its own, which this package neither authors nor can inspect. `request/header` records everything the harness sends and nothing about that wrapper. This is the one place where the route is weaker than a keyed adapter, and it is a property of driving a product rather than an API.

### Keeping the query alive

A query takes seconds before its first token. `includePartialMessages: true` makes the product publish partial assistant events while it works, and those events are what rearm the provider's own idle watchdog, so `queryTimeoutMs` bounds a silent installation rather than the answer's duration — the same posture as the keyed adapters' `streamIdleTimeoutMs`.

Those partials are not forwarded to the seam as chunks. The `StreamChunk` protocol has no block-neutral heartbeat: `BlockAssembler` opens a partial block for any delta, so an empty text delta would put a spurious empty text block in every tool-call-only response and log one `assistant/chunk` per partial. The cost is that first-token time equals whole-answer time for this route, which the stats projection reports honestly.

## Alternatives considered

**The trampoline: let the product's own loop call the harness tools through an in-process MCP server.** Another slice is building exactly that as a bridge in the subagent seam, where it belongs: it gives a delegated task the harness's tools while the product keeps its loop, its session, and its multi-step control. At the LLM seam it would be the wrong shape. `generate()` is one model response, and a trampolined query would run a whole nested agent loop behind it — tool calls the harness never logged as its own steps, budget the session-budget guard never counted, approvals the interaction seam never saw, and a `request/header` that no longer explains the response. Keeping this provider stateless is what makes every harness role work unchanged: the loop stays the harness's, so the read barrier, the plan-mode state, the compaction threshold, and the retry policy all keep meaning what they mean on a keyed route.

**Extend `dsh-subagent-claude-code` instead of adding a package.** The subagent provider answers a different Service Definition — it starts and settles a delegated run — and its capabilities, cancellation, and result vocabulary are the subagent seam's. Sharing a package would fuse two seams' contracts to save one dependency; the two do share the SDK pin and the custom-spawn projection, and that duplication is deliberate and marked, because neither package may depend on the other.

**Ask for tool calls in free text instead of a structured output.** It would remove the schema and the turn the product spends delivering it, but parsing tool calls out of prose is exactly the failure the seam's raw-JSON-argument contract avoids, and a malformed call would be indistinguishable from an answer. The structured output makes a missing or unreadable answer a provider failure with a code, never an empty turn.

**Let the product read the workspace and run its own tools for read-only work.** Cheaper per turn, and wrong: the harness's read barrier, observation policy, and approvals are the reason a tool result is trustworthy. A route that sometimes bypasses them would make the session log an incomplete account of what the agent did.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ctx.llm` serves the configured route end to end from a `cordis.yml` booted through the real Loader, with the SDK's `query` mocked: the route registers, a request returns text and tool-call chunks, and the CLI the SDK asks to spawn goes through the mounted subprocess seam.
- Unit specs hold per-file 100% coverage over `src/`, covering the rendering of a multi-turn conversation with tool calls and results, the tool section, structured-output parsing including tool calls, error mapping, cancellation, idle expiry, the unknown-model refusal, and config validation.
- An opt-in e2e (`DSH_E2E_CLAUDE_CODE=1`) composes `examples/headless-agent` over this route and drives a real installation: the agent creates a file and reads it back through the harness's own bash and editor tools, and the workspace file is verified outside the agent.
- No keyless snapshot accompanies this route. The snapshot harness replays recorded provider transcripts, and this route's provider is a local process whose answers are not recorded; adding one would mean recording the SDK message stream, which is a separate slice. The Loader-booted e2e and the opt-in real run are the evidence until then.

## Risks

**Latency and cost per turn.** Each turn pays the product's start-up plus a full answer, and the whole conversation is re-sent every turn with no prompt caching across turns, so a long session costs full input every step. A deployment with a key should still prefer a keyed route; this one exists for the host that has none.

**The product's envelope.** The system prompt the model actually reads is the harness prompt inside a wrapper this package cannot see or record. Prompt-sensitive behavior — a system-prompt change that a snapshot would pin on a keyed route — is only partly accounted for here.

**Quota.** The queries spend the operator's subscription, and the product reports rate-limit state this route does not yet surface as seam usage. A run that exhausts the subscription fails as a product error the harness retries under the normal policy.

**Turn-bound brittleness.** The bound is two assistant messages. A product-side structured-output retry would exceed it and surface as a failed query; if that proves common the bound is the field to revisit, not the design.

# Agent Notes

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

One kind of design doc lives here. An **Agent Note** records a decision or proposal that affects this codebase — the *why* and *what we gave up*, the parts code and docs can't carry. This file defines where Agent Notes live, when to write one, and [the in-file format](#the-file-format).

## Layout and naming

Every Agent Note has two axes, both encoded in its **path** — `{lifecycle}/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic-title.md`:

- **Lifecycle** (the top-level folder) is the Agent Note's status, and an Agent Note moves between folders as that status changes:
  - **`proposed/`** — proposals reviewed before implementation; not yet built (or only partly).
  - **`implemented/`** — the decision shipped. The file records what was decided and what was rejected, and is **kept current with what actually shipped**: when the code later moves a file, renames a package, or changes a key/default, the Agent Note is updated in the same change to match (facts only — paths, names, structure — not the decision itself). See [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md).
  - **`rejected/`** — the proposal was considered and declined. Keep it only while its rationale prevents a tempting, meaningful mistake; otherwise delete the complete triplet.
- **Class** (the nested folder) is the *kind* of decision — see [Classification](#classification) below.

The date in the filename is when the topic was **first proposed** (per git history). Cross-references between Agent Notes use relative markdown links (`[topic](../../implemented/architecture/2026-…-….md)`) — never bare prose or numbers — so they are mechanically checkable and survive moves between folders.

The active lifecycle tree is the working inventory: browse its lifecycle/class folders or search the repository. Do not add a centralized `INDEX.md`; the [no-index Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-19-remove-generated-agent-note-index.md) owns the rationale. Low-future-value implemented records move to the separate frozen [`archived/`](archived/AGENTS.md) tree described below.

## Classification

Each Agent Note belongs to one path-encoded class from the closed set in `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts`; the classification gate rejects other folders. Adding a class requires updating the canonical set and this section. See the [classification Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-06-20-agent-note-classification.md).

| Class | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `feature` | A new user- or model-facing capability. |
| `bug-fix` | Corrects a defect or closes a gap a postmortem surfaced. |
| `simplification` | Removes code, behavior, or surface area without adding a capability. |
| `architecture` | A structural decision about the **shipped source** — how packages relate, what the runtime vocabulary is. |
| `process` | Tooling, policy, or workflow **around** the code — gates, the package manager, vendoring — not runtime behavior. |
| `testing` | Test infrastructure and strategy. |

The `architecture` / `process` line: **architecture** is about the source we ship; **process** is the surrounding tooling and workflow. (`refactor` is deliberately absent — it overlaps `simplification`, whose discriminator, "does observable behavior change?", already covers it.)

## Archiving and deletion

Archive an implemented Agent Note when the shipped decision is complete and its rationale is unlikely to guide future work. Keep it active when its alternatives, ownership boundary, negative guarantee, durable or wire semantics, security rule, or reintroduction condition remains useful. Never archive a proposed note: reject an obsolete proposal. Keep a rejected note only while it prevents a plausible mistake; otherwise delete its English, Chinese, and sidecar files together. Use the calibrated [`dsh-archive-agent-notes`](../skills/dsh-archive-agent-notes/SKILL.md) workflow rather than word count, age, or a target quota.

The archive is path-encoded as `archived/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic-title.md`; `implemented` is deliberately absent because only implemented notes can enter it. An archival change moves the complete English/Chinese/sidecar triplet, retains `Status: implemented`, inserts the same `Archived: YYYY-MM-DD` line immediately below that status in both language files, re-records the sidecar, and repairs or deletes inbound links. These are the only permitted content changes during archival.

Once sealed, every archived triplet is permanently frozen. Do not edit, translate, reformat, update, move, or delete it, and do not treat it as authority for current behavior. Documentation gates skip archived sources, including their outbound links; active prose may still link into an archived note when it intentionally cites history. [`verify-archived-agent-notes`](../../scripts/verify-archived-agent-notes.ts) enforces the closed class tree, complete triplets, archive metadata, sidecar hashes, and the append-only frozen-content manifest. The [archive-policy Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-26-frozen-agent-note-archive.md) owns the rationale.

## When to write one

Every non-trivial change MUST add or update at least one Agent Note in the same PR. A change is non-trivial when it alters behavior, architecture, a contract shared across files or packages, process or tooling, testing strategy, an on-disk, wire, or configuration format, or another decision a maintainer may reasonably revisit. A proposal for substantial future work starts in `proposed/`; a decision already made starts in `implemented/`. Pick the class folder that matches the decision (see [Classification](#classification)).

Updating the Agent Note that already owns the decision satisfies the rule; do not create a duplicate. Only a purely mechanical or local edit with no change to behavior, contracts, structure, process, or rationale is exempt. An Agent Note is never edited into a *different decision*: supersede it with a new one, and keep both notes cross-linked unless the old note is later fully consolidated under the rule below. Editing an `implemented/` Agent Note to track where its existing decision lives is required, not forbidden; see [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md).

An implemented Agent Note that is fully superseded may be consolidated into the current owning note and deleted. Before deletion, the owner must preserve every unique rationale, alternative, consequence, required verification, and named coverage gap; repair every inbound link; and delete the Chinese counterpart and consistency record in the same change. Partial supersession does not qualify: keep both notes cross-linked and update every fact that remains current. Consolidation must not rewrite the old file into its opposite or rely on git history as the only copy of rationale.

A feature-addition note may be consolidated into the later removal note only when the feature is absent from production code, configuration, schemas, durable or wire formats, migration, and compatibility behavior; no current documentation presents it as available; and no test exercises it as supported behavior. Removal rationale and tests that verify absence may remain. The removal owner preserves the original motivation, why it no longer justified the feature, alternatives to full removal, the capability given up, conditions for reintroduction, and verification of complete absence. Obsolete implementation inventories and tests that only verified the deleted behavior are not current verification evidence. Removing one transport, default, implementation, or presentation is partial supersession, as is any surviving durable data or compatibility handling.

## The file format

Every active Agent Note follows one in-file format, enforced by `pnpm run verify-agent-note-format` ([scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts](../../scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts), part of `doc-sync`); the rationale for the format — and the alternatives it rejected — is [the uniform-format Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-05-uniform-agent-note-format.md). Archived notes retain the format they had when sealed plus the archive-date line above.

### The header block

The first three lines of every Agent Note are exactly:

```markdown
# Agent Note: <title>

Status: <status>
```

followed by a blank line. The `Status:` value is one of three forms, and must agree with the lifecycle folder the file sits in — the gate cross-checks them:

- `Status: proposed`
- `Status: implemented`
- `Status: rejected — <why, in one line>`

The status carries no dates and no parentheticals: the filename holds the first-proposed date, git holds everything else, and an "accepted in amended form" note is body content (state the amendment where the decision is stated). The rejection reason is the one status with content, because a rejected Agent Note's verdict is the fact readers come for.

### The body skeleton

Every Agent Note opens its body with `## Problem` — the motivation, written to stand without the solution. What follows depends on the lifecycle; recurring sections use these canonical names and nothing else, while genuinely bespoke technical sections (package topology, wire contracts, schemas) remain free-form between the required ones.

#### `proposed/`

```markdown
## Problem
## Proposal
…bespoke sections…
## Alternatives considered
## Acceptance criteria
## Risks
```

`## Proposal` is the intended change and may legitimately speak in the future tense — plans, migration steps, and open questions belong here while the work is unbuilt. `## Acceptance criteria` says what observable state means done. `## Risks` covers both what could go wrong and what the change knowingly gives up.

#### `implemented/`

```markdown
## Problem
## Decision
…bespoke sections…
## Alternatives considered
## Consequences
```

`## Decision` describes shipped reality in the present tense, and the whole file is kept current with it per [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md). `## Consequences` records what the trade-off cost **and** bought. Proposal-era headings are spec-speak here and the gate rejects them: `## Proposal`, `## Plan`, `## Migration plan`, and `## Acceptance criteria` may not appear in an implemented Agent Note (the [slop checklist](../../docs/AGENTS.md) names why). A `## Testing`, `## Deferred`, or `## Related` section is fine where it states present-tense fact.

#### `rejected/`

A rejected Agent Note is the proposal, frozen: it keeps whatever proposal-time sections it had (including `## Acceptance criteria` or `## Plan`), and the verdict lives on the `Status:` line. Only the header block, the `## Problem` opener, a `## Proposal` section, and the Alternatives-considered mandate below apply.

### Alternatives considered — mandatory

Every Agent Note carries an `## Alternatives considered` section: each genuine alternative and why it lost, one bold-led paragraph per alternative or a `### Why not <X>?` subsection per contested one. A decision recorded without what it beat invites re-litigation — the failure Agent Notes exist to prevent.

Alternatives are recorded, never invented. An Agent Note dated before 2026-07-05 whose alternatives are not reconstructible from the record carries this exact comment in place of the section, which the gate accepts for pre-format files only:

```markdown
<!-- agent-note-format: alternatives-not-recorded (pre-format Agent Note) -->
```

### Moving between lifecycles
